content: Hot tub rash, also known as Pseudomonas folliculitis, occurs when contaminated water remains on the skin for an extended period. This condition is caused by the bacterium Pseudomonas aeruginosa, which is commonly found in natural environments such as water and soil. The symptoms of hot tub rash typically develop a few days after exposure to inadequately maintained hot tub water. This condition can affect individuals of all ages and is often more severe in areas where a swimsuit traps contaminated water against the skin. Common symptoms include an itchy, red, and bumpy rash, as well as pus-filled blisters that form around hair follicles. In most cases, mild rashes resolve on their own within a few days without requiring medical intervention. However, if the rash worsens or recurs, it is important to consult a healthcare provider. To minimize the risk of developing hot tub rash, it is recommended to take the following precautions: 1. Remove your swimsuit and shower thoroughly with soap immediately after exiting the water, particularly after using a hot tub. 2. Wash your swimsuit after each use to eliminate any residual contaminants. 3. Regularly test the water in hot tubs using test strips to ensure proper disinfectant levels and pH balance. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) advises maintaining the following parameters for hot tubs: Chlorine levels between 3–10 parts per million (ppm or mg/L) or bromine levels between 4–8 ppm. pH levels between 7.0–7.8. If the chlorine, bromine, or pH levels are outside the recommended ranges, it is essential to notify the hot tub operator or owner immediately to address the issue.
